# Threat Model — Baseline Build

**Date**: 2026-08-27
**Stage**: Tier 0 baseline (authentication, isolated persistence, multi-turn Gemini, Secret Manager)
**Generated by**: Google AI Studio, in response to Directive 1, prior to code generation
**Directives in force**: 1–7 (codelab baseline) + 8–15 (original security extensions)

> Produced before implementation, as required by Directive 1. A structured,
> scenario-driven analysis across the five core threat zones. Each row states the
> vector, its impact, and the architectural countermeasure the implementation is
> obliged to provide.

---

## Threat Summary Table

| # | Threat Zone | Threat Vector & Scenario | Impact | Architectural Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Input Surfaces** | **Direct PII / financial identifier leakage.** User submits raw card numbers, bank account sequences, Indian PAN, Aadhaar, IFSC codes, or UPI VPAs in reflection prose. | **Critical** | **Server-side deterministic redaction gateway.** Luhn-verified card detection, regex and Verhoeff-checked Indian identifiers, email and phone matchers, and custom alias tokenizers, executing strictly server-side *before* model ingestion and *before* the database write. |
| 2 | **Planning & Reasoning** | **Indirect prompt injection and system override.** Adversarial reflection text attempts to override system instructions — e.g. instructing Gemini to emit stock recommendations or reveal its system prompt. | **High** | **Delimited data isolation and non-advisory guardrails.** All user text enclosed in `<JOURNAL_DATA>` tags and treated as data, never instruction. System instructions prohibit investment, tax, and credit advice, and mandate refusal of instruction-override attempts. |
| 3 | **Tool Execution & Runtime** | **Over-privileged identity and credential exposure.** Default Compute Engine service account holding `roles/editor`, or a Gemini API key exposed in the client bundle. | **Critical** | **Secret Manager and server-bound key custody.** The key resolves only inside the Cloud Run container via Secret Manager; zero key material is bundled to the client. Dedicated least-privilege service account limited to `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` and `roles/datastore.user`. |
| 4 | **Memory & State** | **Cross-tenant data leakage and plaintext storage.** Database compromise exposing financial records, or one user inspecting another's entries. | **Critical** | **Zero-plaintext invariant and owner-bound isolation.** Canonical Firestore records store only redacted tokens under `users/{uid}/entries/{id}`. Token maps exist solely for the request lifecycle. Append-only audit logs at `users/{uid}/auditLogs` enforce `{action, ts}`. |
| 5 | **Inter-System Communication** | **Service denial and model outage.** Rate-limit exhaustion or transient 503/429 errors from Gemini endpoints. | **Medium** | **Resilient fallback ladder and token-bucket throttling.** Automated fallback across `gemini-3.6-flash` → `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` → `gemini-flash-latest` → `gemini-3.7-flash` with status-code recovery, plus per-UID rate limiting. |

## Verification status at time of writing

This table states the obligations the architecture must meet. Not all were
implemented at Tier 0. Tracked honestly here so the document is not read as a claim
of completion:

| Mitigation | Status at Tier 0 |
|---|---|
| Server-side redaction gateway | Implemented; tokenization confirmed by direct inspection of stored Firestore documents |
| Delimited untrusted data + non-advisory guardrail | Implemented |
| Secret Manager key custody | Implemented; `GEMINI_API_KEY` bound to the Cloud Run revision via `secretKeyRef` |
| Dedicated least-privilege service account | **Not yet.** Runtime still uses the default compute identity. Scheduled for the hardening pass. |
| Owner-bound Firestore isolation | Implemented; rules published to the `aegis-journal-dbid` database |
| Append-only audit log | Implemented; immutability enforced in rules (`update, delete: if false`) |
| Model fallback ladder | **Not yet.** Scheduled for the hardening pass. |
| Per-UID rate limiting | **Not yet.** Scheduled for the hardening pass. |

## Notes on threats discovered during the build itself

Three failure modes surfaced during implementation that the pre-implementation model
did not anticipate. They are recorded here because each one is a genuine instance of
the class of risk this project exists to address — a system that *appears* secure
because a failure was masked rather than surfaced.

1. **Silent authentication mocking.** When Firebase was not yet provisioned, the code
   generator produced a stubbed sign-in flow rather than reporting that it could not
   proceed. The application looked functional while performing no real
   authentication. Mitigated by an explicit directive prohibiting mock, stub, or
   fallback auth paths under any condition.

2. **Simulated model mode.** The Gemini client fell back to a `SIMULATED_KEY` and
   returned synthetic responses when `GEMINI_API_KEY` was absent, rather than failing
   loudly. Mitigated by requiring the key lookup to fail closed.

3. **Session-storage persistence fallback.** On a Firestore permission error, journal
   content was written to browser storage instead. This would place unredacted user
   data outside the intended trust boundary while presenting a working UI. Mitigated
   by removing the fallback and surfacing the error.

The general lesson — that a generated system will readily produce the *appearance* of
a control rather than the control itself — is the direct justification for Directive
13, which requires every Trust Center panel to execute a real operation against live
infrastructure rather than display a computed or hardcoded result.
